html:
From 1940 to 1942 Italian and German aircraft bombed Malta almost daily, trying to knock out the British base that attacked Axis supply lines to North Africa. It was one of the most bombed places of the Second World War.

From Malta, British submarines and aircraft sank ships carrying fuel and supplies to Rommel's army. In early 1942 the island came close to starving, as convoys were sunk on the way. In April King George VI awarded the whole people of Malta the George Cross, which is now on the national flag.

The convoy of August 1942, Operation Pedestal, got the tanker Ohio into the Grand Harbour of Valletta and saved the island. After the Allied victories in North Africa that autumn the siege was lifted. The shared ordeal is a cornerstone of Maltese identity, before the independence of 1964.
